title: The Thorn of the Glass Steppe
premise: Edmund Almeida has spent five years hiding her magic in the city of Vell, where a royal edict made spellcraft punishable by burning—until her date, a quiet archivist named Sera, turns out to be pictured in a century-old book of prophecies that also names Edmund as the one who will 'unmake the crown.' The prophecy's true meaning is darker than it seems: King Aldous was replaced years ago by a hollow thing called the Regent, sustained by stolen memories harvested from magically gifted citizens, and Edmund's own missing childhood memories are woven into its core. As Edmund and Sera race to unbind the king before the Regent completes its harvest of the city's last hidden mages—including Edmund herself—they discover that destroying the Regent means sacrificing the only intact memory Edmund has left: her mother's face. In the end, Edmund chooses truth over wholeness, frees the real king from his century-long enchantment, and finds that belonging was never something she lost—it was something she finally stopped running from.
about_author: X. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing rare grimoires before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about people whose magic costs more than they can afford, and live somewhere with too many books and not enough shelves.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She sells a luck-knot to a dockworker in Vell's night market, hiding her craft behind mundane trinkets. A patrol nearly catches her; she escapes through alleys she knows by heart. The beat establishes her careful invisibility and the loneliness beneath it—she helps people feel safe while trusting no one herself.

chapters.title: The Girl with Ink-Stained Fingers
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Her date with Sera, a palace archive clerk, goes unexpectedly well—until Sera mentions a strange book no one can catalogue. Edmund feels an old dread stir. The emotional beat is tentative hope: for the first time in five years, Edmund wants to be known, and that wanting terrifies her.

chapters.title: A Century of Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Sera shows her the prophecy book: a watercolor portrait of Sera herself, dated 112 years ago, beside a verse about 'the thorn' who will 'unmake the crown.' Edmund recognizes her own hedge-witch sigil in the margins. Panic and wonder collide; her safe life ends on this page.

chapters.title: What the Edict Burned
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She reveals why she sought Edmund out: gifted citizens have been vanishing for months, all quietly erased from records. Sera suspects the palace itself. The beat is reluctant alliance—two women who trust no institutions deciding to trust each other anyway.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Using a scrying charm, they glimpse King Aldous at a public rite—and see the wrongness beneath him: a flickering, hungry presence wearing his face like a mask. Edmund recognizes the magic as memory-work, the same discipline her mother taught her. Dread becomes purpose.

chapters.title: Mother's Grammar
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, with flashbacks. Digging out her mother's old spellbook, Edmund confronts gaps in her own memory—five years ago is a blur, and so is most of her childhood. The beat is grief sharpening into resolve: whatever took her past is connected to the thing on the throne.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They break into the sealed sub-archive and find ledgers of 'harvests'—names, dates, and recorded memories extracted from mages, including an entry for E. Almeida, five years old. Sera realizes Edmund is both investigator and victim. Betrayal of self by history; fury kindles.

chapters.title: The Regent's Smile
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Summoned—or trapped—by a royal writ, Edmund stands before the king. The Regent speaks to her privately, knowing her name, offering to return her memories if she stops digging. The temptation is exquisite; the beat is the first taste of how much the enemy understands her.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Lie
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera is approached by her archive superior, who reveals he has been feeding names to the palace to protect his own daughter. He asks Sera to do the same. Torn between protecting Edmund and protecting family, Sera lies to both. Guilt becomes a ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Thorn Prophecy, Read Backwards
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Deciphering the prophecy's mirrored second half, Edmund learns the 'unmaking' requires a living anchor—a mage bound willingly to the Regent's core. Every previous candidate died screaming. The beat is cold clarity: the prophecy isn't a destiny, it's a warning label.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Hiding with a network of outlawed hedge-mages, Edmund experiences belonging for the first time—shared meals, shared spells. But the community's leader wants to use Edmund as bait. Warmth curdles into being-used; Edmund must decide what loyalty deserves.

chapters.title: What Sera Gave Away
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The safehouse is raided; the leader is taken. Edmund discovers Sera's report made it possible—not betrayal by intent, but by coercion. Confrontation in the rain. The beat is heartbreak without hatred: Edmund chooses to believe Sera over her own fear, and hates herself for it.

chapters.title: Into the Harvest
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. To redeem herself, Sera volunteers to be harvested—entering the palace's memory-vault under cover of a routine extraction—to map the Regent's core from inside. Inside, she finds fragments of Edmund's stolen childhood. Sacrifice as apology; terror as devotion.

chapters.title: The Face in the Vault
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Following Sera's smuggled map, Edmund breaches the vault and finds her mother's extracted memories—alive, luminous, archived. She can restore them or use them as a weapon against the Regent, but not both. The chapter's beat is the cruelest choice of the book, deferred but not escaped.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was King
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Deep in the vaults they find the real Aldous—alive, aged, enchanted into stillness for decades. His fragmentary testimony reveals the Regent was created by his own fear of usurpation. Sympathy complicates rage: the monster was invited in.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The Regent offers final terms: Edmund's memories returned whole, Sera spared, the city's mages left alone—if Edmund binds herself as the anchor willingly. Edmund sees the trap inside the gift. The beat is terrible maturity: some bargains must be refused even when every alternative hurts.

chapters.title: Nightfall on the Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The Regent, refused, begins a forced harvest of the entire city—streets filling with blank-eyed citizens. Edmund and Sera rally the hedge-mages for a desperate assault on the palace. The beat is unity forged under fire: the invisible made visible at last.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the throne, Edmund begins the unbinding ritual while Sera holds the line below. The Regent fights back with Edmund's own stolen memories, weaponizing her mother's voice. The climax's first movement: love used as a blade, and surviving it.

chapters.title: The Price of Wholeness
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The ritual demands the sacrifice foretold: Edmund feeds her last intact memory—her mother's face—into the core, collapsing the Regent from within. She destroys it weeping. The beat is grief transmuted into choice: truth over comfort, freely given.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Crown
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The real Aldous wakes to a changed kingdom; the harvest victims begin remembering themselves, Edmund among them—except for the hole where her mother was. Public reckoning begins. The beat is exhaustion and fragile relief: survival without triumph.

chapters.title: The Empty Page
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The prophecy book's final page now shows Edmund and Sera together—and then the ink fades, unwriting itself. Prophecy fulfilled is prophecy ended. Edmund realizes her future belongs to no text but her own. Quiet hope; authorship of self.

chapters.title: Roots Above Ground
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, epilogue. Magic is decriminalized; Edmund teaches hedge-craft openly, her mother's grammar passed on though the face is gone. Sera stays. Standing in the rebuilt night market, Edmund understands belonging was never found—it was built. The story closes on warmth earned, not granted.
